summary: The plan is honest, low-risk, and correctly avoids repeating the rejected layout/printed-percentage ideas - but as designed it does not actually make the biggest leak measurable, which is its entire purpose. The two new claim events carry no email and no operation_id, so the person-linking tool the plan promises to run next cycle returns 0-of-0; a durable per-visitor identifier must be added to all three claim events before this is worth building.

findings.issue: The plan's headline deliverable - two 'person-linked, frozen, significance-tested' sub-funnels via tools/linked-funnel.mjs (page_viewed -> email_field_engaged, and email_field_engaged -> email_entered) - cannot be computed with the events as designed. linked-funnel.mjs identifies a person ONLY by email, falling back to operation_id; rows with neither are UNLINKABLE and are excluded from the denominator. On the claim page, page_viewed (claim.html:1178-1183) and the proposed email_field_engaged (fired at email-field FOCUS, before any email is typed) both carry email=null and no operation_id. So both 'from' events are 100% unlinkable and every promised command resolves to 0/0.
findings.evidence: Read tools/linked-funnel.mjs lines 17, 52 (who = email || operation_id || null), 76 (unlinkableFrom++ when no id), 87 (den = firstFrom.size). Read claim.html: page_viewed POST (1176-1184) sends only event/phase/role:unknown/product/source/properties - no email, no operationId; email_entered POST (1306-1314) sends email. Grep of claim.html for operationId/session_id/visitorId/uuid: none exist at page-view or focus time (only state.sku). PROOF - ran the plan's own next-cycle command against live Supabase: `node --experimental-websocket tools/linked-funnel.mjs page_viewed email_entered 14 --until=2026-07-20 --compare` -> 'page_viewed -> email_entered, linked per person: 0 of 0 = -%' and '14 page_viewed rows (100%) had no email/operation_id - excluded'. email_field_engaged fires even earlier (empty field) so it will be identically unlinkable.
findings.required_fix: Attach a durable, stable per-visitor identifier to ALL THREE claim events (page_viewed, email_field_engaged, email_entered) in a field linked-funnel keys on - e.g. set operationId to a client-generated UUID persisted for the visit, or to posthog.get_session_id()/get_distinct_id() (already available in the claim.html PostHog stub), OR extend linked-funnel to link on a session id in properties. Then dry-run the two promised commands and confirm they return non-zero linked denominators BEFORE shipping. Without this, the events can only be divided as raw counts - the exact ratio-of-two-event-counts anti-pattern the changelog and linked-funnel were built to forbid.

findings.issue: The plan states the top-of-funnel is unmeasurable this cycle only because page_viewed is 2 days old and PostHog is 403 - but omits that page_viewed is ALSO permanently unlinkable in linked-funnel for lack of any person key. Even after it accumulates two weeks, it still cannot be person-linked as currently emitted. The freshness caveat masks the linking defect.
findings.evidence: plan.json measurement_caveats[2] and leaks_ranked[0].prior_rate attribute the gap to the 2-day age of durable page_viewed; they never mention that page_viewed carries no email/operation_id. Confirmed by the live 0/0 run above (100% unlinkable, independent of window age).
findings.required_fix: Acknowledge the linking defect explicitly and fix it (same identifier fix as the critical finding); do not carry forward the implication that time alone makes page_viewed measurable in a person-linked way.
